title: Tract Mirror — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Tract Mirror's rich face: the walk from one joint up to the mirror run backward, the proofs the build already made laid beside the claims they back, and the fingerprint of the words each piece was made against. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.title: a short melody · the C++ engine, offline
pieces.caption: The plugin's own engine singing a legato line with glide and vibrato, rendered by its offline harness (TractMirrorRender, 48 kHz), not recorded in Live. One voice at a time: each new note takes the tube from the last.

pieces.file: Tract Mirror — rich — junction to mirror.html
pieces.title: one joint, then the whole mirror
pieces.caption: **The claim, walked up and then run backward.** One joint between two tubes and the power it splits; a straight tube that rings at its quarter-wave notes; a shaped tube that says a vowel; a morph; and last, linear prediction reading the tube back out of its own sound. With the glottis closed and no loss the ladder comes back joint for joint (largest gap under 10⁻¹¹ on all six vowels). With the plugin's leaky glottis (+0.97) and lossy walls (0.996 per joint) it comes back as a different tube, up to 0.25 off on /a/ and 0.61 on /o/, whose sound has the same shape, within 2 × 10⁻¹³ of its peak, once one overall level is matched: the read-back tube plays 12 dB louder on /a/ and 16 dB on /o/. Either condition alone, the leak or the wall loss, is enough to break the identity. Every tube is read from vowels.json; the checks beside it re-run each step's numbers against the Python reference.

verdicts.file: Tract Mirror — rich — junction to mirror.html
verdicts.why: A real test that walks up cleanly and runs clean; fix two wordings only. 'Same sound, sample for sample' hides a fitted gain (0.250 /a/, 0.153 /o/ as shipped, read-back ~12-16 dB louder): say 'once one overall level is matched' and print the gain (html line 650, the #r5same label at line 208, and the manifest caption); and line 650's 'what you assume about the ends' should be 'the ends and the walls' (loss 0.996 alone gives /o/ a 0.628 gap). Optional: lip −0.738 = 0.97 × 0.9 × 0.996^42.

The build's full instrument, reached after the walk that is its way up; clean, silent until a click. Note: 1600 px under the same paragraph as the 1150 px walk, with its stale first-version review panel; collapsing it is Loudon's taste.

Decoration beside step 4 of the walk, which plays the same a-i-u morph live, draws every k and tests the recompute. Its 'the synth's own sound' is also loose: make_clips.py builds on kl_reference, not the plugin.

pieces.title: the six area functions
pieces.caption: The six fitted tubes as silhouettes, glottis left, lips right, radius √(A/π). The optimizer chose a cosine series, 19 coefficients per vowel; these are the 64 points it draws, clipped at 12 cm² (the flat tops on /a/, /i/, /o/ and /u/). Everything else is derived from them.

pieces.title: the glottal source
pieces.caption: One period of the Rosenberg pulse as tension changes, and its spectrum tilting; breath lifts the noise floor. This is what excites the tube before any vowel exists.

verdicts.why: Shows the single source of truth the section names. Caption note: the optimizer chose 19 cosine coefficients (fit_vowels.py:6,38) clipped at 12 cm² (:37); the 64 points are what they draw, and the flat tops are the clip.
The only piece that isolates the excitation the text names in one phrase, with its spectrum; the frame matches the caption.
Half of a real ear test of the single-source claim (Python, 44.1 kHz, 22 sections); caption matches make_renders.py:90,95.

The other half (C++, 48 kHz, 24 sections, vibrato and breath zeroed per RenderHarness.cpp:89-92); CMakeLists.txt:18-25 embeds vowels.json, and both web artifacts carry all six curves and five constants, re-checked.
Backs 'Verified in Live 12'; the caption says exactly what the build log does (VST3 loaded, AU through auval), and the image shows plugin mode, /i/, r_g +0.97, r_l −0.90.

offers.what: The identity is exact only in the ideal tube, and the ideal takes two conditions: a closed glottis and lossless walls. The walk's last step runs LPC (Levinson-Durbin, order 44) on the tube's own click. With both conditions the reflection coefficients come back equal to the area-ratio k at every joint (largest gap under 10⁻¹¹ on six vowels, lip rung −0.900). As shipped (glottis +0.97, loss 0.996 per joint) they come back as a different tube whose sound has the same shape once one overall level is matched (within 2 × 10⁻¹³; the read-back tube is 12 dB louder on /a/, 16 dB on /o/). Gaps: 0.254 /a/, 0.124 /e/, 0.117 /i/, 0.612 /o/, 0.158 /u/, 0 schwa. Either condition alone breaks it: for /o/, the leak alone gives 0.401 and the loss alone 0.628. The lip rung reads −0.7377, exactly 0.97 × 0.9 × 0.996⁴², the round trip's losses gathered into the last rung (the challenger's Python recompute confirms every figure). Offer: name both conditions where the opening says the LPC coefficients are the impedance mismatches. It bears on the v2 analysis engine: a singer's tract read back from their sound will draw both glottal leak and wall loss as shape unless they are modelled.

"Verified in Ableton Live 12, VST3 + AU" says more than the build log does. Phase 4 (build plan :68) records that Live listed both formats and that the VST3 was loaded and played (renders/ableton-proof.png); the AU passed auval (:63) and was never loaded in Live. And the Live check came before Phases 5 and 6: the build plan has the in-Live MIDI re-verification pending (:82), and the scroll says the MIDI controls and Word mode have not been played inside Ableton (scroll :47). Offer: "Verified in Ableton Live 12 on 2026-06-10 (VST3; the AU passes auval)", or load the AU and the later build once and keep the words.

A fix in the bundle, not the page. renders/clips/clip_scattering_junction.mp4 labels its arrows "transmitted (1+k)/2" and "reflected |k|" (renders/make_clips.py:519-520), so at k = −0.051 it reads 47 % on and 5 % back, and the caption calls that energy. The walk's first step shows the right sums: pressure on 1+k, back k; power on 1−k², back k², adding to 1. The clip is left out of this face until it is re-rendered with those labels.
